title: Carry a loaded litter to the trolley: lift and lower both ends together, level
instruction: Lift the grey litter by both handles at the same time, keep it level, carry it forward and lower it onto the dark grey trolley, both ends together, then let go. Do not drag the litter and do not lift one end before the other. The orange casualty must stay on the litter.
context: Two-bearer litter and stretcher carries by EMTs and paramedics (O*NET 29-2042 and 29-2043) and patient transfers by nursing assistants (31-1131), and any two-person lift of a long load: the bearers lift and lower together on a count and keep the litter level, because a litter raised or set down at one end first tips the patient, and a litter dragged along the ground instead of lifted clear injures the patient and the bearers. Here the litter is too long to lift at its centre (the casualty covers the middle) and lifting it by one end tilts it, so the job is two-handed by physics, and the rule (ends together, level, both hands on it in the air, never dragged, lowered gently) is scored over the whole trial, not only from where the litter ends up.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three objects. (1) Litter: a loose flat board of pale grey rigid polymer, 500 mm long (along y), 40 mm wide (along x), 20 mm thick, 0.20 kg, lying flat on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y 0, long side along y, so its ends are at y -25.0 cm and +25.0 cm; its outer 100 mm at each end (|y| 15.0 to 25.0 cm) are the handles. (2) Casualty: a loose box of orange rigid plastic standing in for the patient, 300 mm along y, 70 mm along x, 40 mm tall, 0.30 kg, lying centred on the litter (centre x 24.0 cm, y 0, its underside on the litter's top 20 mm above the table), sides parallel to x and y; it overhangs the litter by 15 mm on each x side and covers the litter's middle 300 mm, so a gripper can take the litter only by its handles. (3) Trolley: a fixed dark grey rigid platform standing in for an ambulance trolley's deck, 120 mm along x, 360 mm along y, 30 mm tall, fixed to the table centred at x 38.0 cm, y 0 (it spans x 32.0 to 44.0 cm, y -18.0 to +18.0 cm), sides parallel to x and y. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the litter and the casualty and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). Definitions. 'End heights' are the heights of the bottom edge of each 40 x 20 mm end face of the litter (the mean of that face's two lower corners); 'end difference' is how much they differ. 'Tilt' is the angle of the litter's long axis from the horizontal; 'flat' is the angle of its broad face from the horizontal (either face may be down). The surface under the litter is the trolley's top when the litter's centre is over the trolley's 120 x 360 mm footprint, else the table top; 'clearance' is the litter's lowest point's height above that surface. 'Resting on the trolley': its centre over the trolley and its lowest point within 3 mm of the trolley's top. 'An end is up': either end's bottom edge at least 10 mm above the table top. 'Low': its lowest point less than 10 mm above the table top, or, while any part of its outline is over the trolley, less than 10 mm above the trolley's top. 'Drag' is the horizontal travel of the litter's centre summed over the steps on which it is low, followed in steps of 0.5 mm so that contact jitter does not add up. 'Casualty on the litter': the casualty's underside within 6 mm of the litter's top, its centre within 30 mm of the litter's centre horizontally, and it tilted less than 10 degrees. 'Carried level': at some step the litter's lowest point at least 30 mm above the table top, its tilt under 5 degrees, its end difference at most 20 mm, and the casualty on it. A gripper 'holds' the litter when its opening is under 0.9 and its finger zone (every point within the fingers' outer-corner radius of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper) is within 10 mm of the litter; it has 'let go' otherwise. 'Set-down speed' is the litter's fastest downward speed while over the trolley within 10 mm above it before it comes to rest, counting on the step it comes to rest how far it came down in that step. Score 0 if at any moment: the drag exceeds 15 mm (the litter was dragged along the table or the trolley); the casualty is not on the litter for 5 control steps in a row (0.25 s; a one-step contact hop as the litter is lifted or set down does not count), or tilts more than 15 degrees; the litter's tilt exceeds 10 degrees; the end difference exceeds 40 mm while an end is up (lifted or lowered at one end); the litter's clearance is 10 mm or more while a gripper is not holding it (carried or thrown with one hand); or if either object ends off the table (lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise, at the last step: 1.0 if the litter rests flat on the trolley (resting on it, flat within 3 degrees, long axis along the trolley's within 10 degrees, centre within 15 mm of the trolley's centre in x and 20 mm in y), the casualty is on it, both grippers have let go, and over the trial the end difference never exceeded 20 mm and the tilt never exceeded 5 degrees while an end was up and the set-down speed never exceeded 0.10 m/s; 0.75 if the litter rests flat on the trolley with its centre within 40 mm in x and in y and the casualty on it, but not all of the 1.0 conditions (lifted or lowered unevenly by 20 to 40 mm, tilted 5 to 10 degrees, dropped the last way onto the trolley, further off centre, or a gripper still holding); 0.5 if the litter rests on the trolley (lowest point within 3 mm of its top, centre over it, flat within 10 degrees) with the casualty on it, but not meeting 0.75 (turned, rolled on an edge, or its centre more than 40 mm off); 0.25 if the litter was carried level at some moment but is not on the trolley at the end (set back on the table, or still held); 0 in every other case (never lifted clear, or lifted under 30 mm). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both objects still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, 'both grippers hold it' and 'both have let go' are taken as met. In a real trial: side video of each end against cards standing upright behind the litter's path (out of the arms' way) marked at 10, 20 and 40 mm above the bench and at 10, 20 and 40 mm above the trolley's deck, for the end heights and their difference; the drag from the same video against a 15 mm mark on the bench beside the litter's starting place; a top photo of the end state against centre lines taped on the trolley's deck 15 and 40 mm either side of its centre in x and 20 and 40 mm in y; the set-down from the video's last frames before contact against the 10 mm mark.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The trolley is a fixed block; the litter is a uniform rigid board with no poles, handles or straps (its end sections are the handles only by position), and the casualty a uniform rigid box resting on it under its own weight and friction, not strapped. The two bearers are the station's two arms, which lift from above with parallel grippers rather than carrying at hip height. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round, wider than the real fingers across their closing direction. The arms sag a few millimetres under the shared 0.5 kg load (no payload compensation), which the thresholds allow for.
reset_notes: Put the litter back flat on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y 0, long side along y, and the casualty back centred on it, sides parallel to x and y; the trolley is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
